missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Шляпа' stays in the nominative case as the subject. 'Эта' points at a specific one, and 'красивая' is the agreeing feminine adjective. A clean model for describing an object.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Шляпу' is the accusative direct object of 'купил'. 'Новую' agrees in the feminine accusative, and 'вчера' sets the time. Useful for shopping language.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Шляпы' takes the genitive after 'нет' to express not having something. 'Тёплой' agrees in the feminine genitive. The standard pattern for lacking an item.

missions.phrase: Он подошёл к девушке в шляпе.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'В шляпе' uses the prepositional form 'шляпе' after 'в' to describe what someone is wearing. A natural way to identify a person by their clothing.

Strategic focus: Accusative gift with dative recipient. 'Шляпу' is the accusative direct object, while 'сестре' is the dative recipient. 'Красную' agrees in feminine accusative. A useful giving frame.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of location. 'Шляпой' takes the instrumental after 'под' to show position beneath. 'Этой' agrees in the feminine instrumental. Good for spatial description.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after a quantifier. 'Шляп' is the genitive plural after 'много'. 'Разных' agrees in the genitive plural. A common pattern for describing quantity and variety.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Шляпы' is the nominative plural subject of 'лежат'. 'Эти' agrees in the plural, and 'на полке' gives the location. Useful for describing several items.

Strategic focus: Dative experiencer with nominative subject. 'Шляпа' is nominative, the thing that pleases. 'Мне' is the dative experiencer and 'нравится' agrees with the hat. Highly reusable in speech.

missions.phrase: Я долго искал свою шляпу дома.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative object of searching. 'Шляпу' is the accusative direct object of 'искал'. 'Свою' agrees in the feminine accusative, and 'долго' adds duration. A natural everyday scene.
